adds.title: LGBT rights in Colombia - Wikipedia
adds.summary: National-framework article governing what a visitor stands under in Magdalena, whose own dossier records no department-specific trans finding. It records that consensual same-sex activity has been legal since 1981; Congress passed a law banning discrimination based on sexual orientation in 2011; the right to change legal gender has existed since 1993, and since 2015 gender change is possible without psychiatric or physical evaluations. The Constitutional Court legalized same-sex marriage in April 2016 (fourth Latin American country) and granted same-sex couples full adoption rights in 2015; transgender people have been allowed to serve openly in the military since 2015. It also reports Colombian society as 'generally conservative' on LGBT issues, with an October 2019 Invamer poll reaching 50% support for same-sex marriage for the first time (47% opposed). The article carries no Magdalena-specific fact, so like the record's existing CNN and Guardian sources it grounds the national framework a visitor in this department stands under rather than a department-level finding.
